請撤回 kfx fork 的 tool-result eviction，恢復目前分支所基於的 upstream context 管理行為，並更新 FORK.md，保留歷史與決策紀錄。

## 工作位置與授權

預期分支：refactor-remove-eviction

先確認路徑、分支、HEAD 與 Git 狀態。不要帶入其未提交變更，也不要覆蓋使用者的修改。

這次授權修改檔案與驗證，不授權 commit、push、改寫歷史、開 PR 或安裝至使用者環境。

此 repo 會 rebase 上游，上游迭代速度很快，實作時以 codebase 現況為主

## 先讀

- AGENTS.md
- FORK.md
- kfx/specs/context-budget.md
- kfx/specs/threshold-eviction.md

文件提供歷史背景；實際修改以目前程式與 Git 差異為準。

## 目標與決策理由

優先順序：
1. Agent 的正確性、指示遵循與任務成果。
2. 控制 context amplification 與增長速度。

Eviction 原本依 byte threshold 與 recent-step window，將較舊的工具結果替換成可重新讀取的 handle stub，只修改模型 request，保留 canonical history。

這次決定撤回它，原因是：
- 結果的年齡不代表重要性；skill 指示、程式碼、錯誤證據及 subagent 結果可能仍有用途。
- 先前實測發現 eviction 會把已載入的 skill 全文移出後續 request。
- 替換舊結果會改變 prompt prefix，可能降低 cache 命中並增加重新讀取。
- Eviction 先縮小 request，可能延後 upstream compaction。
- 已有縮小 request 的證據，但沒有證明它改善 agent 成果。
- Upstream 已有工具結果限制、儲存／retrieval 與 automatic compaction，先使用 upstream 既有流程。

這是移除 fork 機制的決策，不是「移除後 agent 表現一定更好」的已驗證結論。

## 實作原則與範圍

目標是撤回 eviction 引入及後續維護的差異，不是重新實作一套沒有 eviction 的 context 管理。

確認目前分支所基於的 upstream revision，以它為還原基準；不要順便更新 upstream。自行依 Git 歷史、差異及 caller 關係判斷需要撤回的程式、測試、設定與共用改動，不照舊文件猜測接點。

撤回後：
- 不再有 fork 的 tool-result eviction。
- FX_KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS 與 FX_EVICT_THRESHOLD_KB 不再影響行為。
- Upstream prompt assembly、compaction、結果限制、儲存與 retrieval 行為保留。
- 其他 fork 功能及修補保留。

不要整份覆蓋含有其他 fork 修改的共用檔案。尤其不得移除 transient tool-call、provider-attempt、recovery checkpoint 或 compaction scratch arena 的記憶體修補。

不要新增替代 eviction、摘要或 context 管理機制，也不要順便重構其他功能。

不要修改使用者的 shell、profile 或 settings；舊環境變數的清理只在交付時提醒。

## 文件與歷史

更新 FORK.md 及直接受影響的 fork-owned 文件。README.md、CHANGELOG.md 等 upstream 文件保持不變。

FORK.md 應：
- 從現行功能、建議設定與 active patch inventory 移除 eviction。
- 取消未來 rebase 或其他功能必須重新接上 eviction 的指示。
- 加入清楚標示「已移除，僅供歷史參考」的紀錄。
- 記錄當初解決的問題、原本的運作方式、本次移除理由，以及移除後使用的 upstream 機制。
- 提供相關文件連結與實際查得的 Git revision，不猜 hash。
- 同步整理 spec index，不將歷史設計列為現行功能或待實作需求。

保留 context-budget.md 與 threshold-eviction.md 中有價值的歷史量測。Eviction 相關內容標示為歷史，不刪除仍有效的其他內容，也不把舊量測當成目前 upstream 的比較結果。歷史命令可以保留但須明示已失效及適用的舊版本


記錄未來若再次遇到 context 增長問題，應先區分單次結果過大、重複讀取、工具／子任務數量、compaction 失效、cache reset 與 process memory retention，再依量測規劃解法，不直接恢復按年齡清結果

## 驗證

依 repo 規範執行 focused checks、build、格式檢查與必要的 runtime 驗證；優先沿用現有 harness，補上必要的回歸測試。

驗證重點：
- 相對還原基準的 eviction 差異已撤回，其他 fork 差異未被誤刪。
- 即使設定舊 eviction 環境變數，仍不會按結果年齡替換正文。
- 已載入的 skill 全文不會在 compaction 前因工具步數增加而被 eviction 移除；不要求 compaction 後永久保留全文。
- Upstream automatic compaction 能觸發並繼續任務。
- 原有大型結果儲存與 read_tool_result 路徑仍正常。正常的 preview 或 handle 不算 eviction。

使用這個 worktree freshly-built 的 ./zig-out/bin/fx，在隔離 HOME 與測試資料下，以 deterministic fake provider 驗證，不使用真實帳號或修改 live profile。

確認退出碼、stderr 與實際結果，不以 build 成功代替 runtime 驗證。若新增 E2E owner，依 repo 規範處理 corpus classification。

Fake provider 只能證明流程行為，不能證明真實 agent 成果或成本改善。若 Full CI 未執行，明確回報，不宣稱已通過完整交付門檻。

## 交付

回報：
- 採用的 upstream 還原基準。
- 撤回的差異，以及保留的其他 fork 機制。
- FORK.md 歷史紀錄的位置。
- 實際執行的驗證、結果與剩餘缺口。
- 舊環境變數已無作用，可由使用者自行清理的提醒

# Unslop

AI voice isn't one mistake — it's a register: throat-clearing, then hype, then hedging, then a summary of what was just said, all in matching triads. The cure is the technical-writing voice of the Google developer docs guide: direct, concrete, second person, zero ceremony. A reader should not be able to tell the text was machine-written.

## The sentence

- Answer first. The first sentence does the job the reader came for; context comes after, if at all.
- Active voice, concrete verb, named actor. Present tense.
- One claim per sentence, committed. "May potentially help" is two hedges on a claim you should either make or drop.
- Plain words carry the confidence. If a noun needs a hype adjective, replace the adjective with the measurement: not "blazingly fast", but "40ms".
- Cut "simply", "easily", "just", "basically", "please" — if it were simple, the sentence wouldn't need to say so.

## The words

Delete on sight; each entry names the usual repair.

| Tell | Repair |
|---|---|
| "Certainly!", "Great question", "I'd be happy to" | start with the answer |
| "It's important/worth noting that X" | "X." |
| "In today's fast-paced / ever-evolving world" | delete the sentence |
| delve, leverage, harness, unlock, empower, foster, elevate, streamline, supercharge | the plain verb: use, run, add, improve |
| seamless, robust, comprehensive, cutting-edge, powerful, game-changing | the specific property, or nothing |

1 	# Threshold-triggered result eviction
2 	
3 	Status: landed, kept for the measurements. Replaces the per-batch advance inside the landed result-eviction patch ([context-budget.md](context-budget.md) feature 1) with a byte-threshold trigger. One file changes: `src/core/agent/runtime/result_eviction.zig`, plus its `State.init` call site in the orchestrator.
4 	
5 	## Problem
6 	
7 	Batch eviction trades cache for context. With `FX_KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS=4`, the eviction boundary advances once per 4 steps, and every advance changes the projected prefix, so the provider prompt cache falls back to the stable ~20K-token system prefix.
8 	
9 	Measured on 2026-09-01, session `08b7ba7e` (real Codex, `gpt-5.6-sol`, 23 requests, 1.10M input):
10	
11	| Request | Context (input delta) | Cache hit fell to | Fresh tokens paid |
12	| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
13	| 9 | 48,947 | 19,968 | 28,979 |
14	| 13 | 62,828 | 19,968 | 42,860 |
15	| 17 | 30,779 | 19,968 | 10,811 |
16	| 20, 21 | ~39,000 | 19,968 | ~19,000 each |
17	
18	Overall cache hit was 77% (253K fresh of 1.10M). The same-prompt A/B on 2026-08-30 measured Claude Code at 92% and Pi at 88%; both leave the prefix untouched within a turn. Amp goes further, letting context grow to 90% of the 272K window before compacting, and runs fine on the same Codex subscription: resending cached tokens is cheap, changing the prefix is what costs. The eviction patch as landed pays that cost every `N` steps for a context ceiling the turn usually does not need.
19	
20	## Design
21	
22	Keep the eviction machinery; change only when the boundary advances.
23	
24	- `FX_KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS=N` keeps its meaning: the newest `N` steps survive a sweep verbatim, and `0` disables eviction entirely.
25	- `FX_EVICT_THRESHOLD_KB=T` (new, default 256) sets the trigger: when the tool-result bytes in the un-evicted part of the suffix, excluding the newest `N` steps, reach `T` KiB, one sweep advances `evicted_before` past everything except those newest `N` steps.
26	
27	Between sweeps the projected prefix is byte-identical, so the cache keeps hitting for as long as the threshold allows, the Amp property, while the sweep still bounds the request body the way the batch version did. 256 KiB of result bytes is roughly 65 to 85K tokens on top of the ~20K stable prefix, well inside the 272K window; a turn like today's (about 40 KB of results per step) sweeps once or twice instead of resetting the prefix four times.
28	
29	Unchanged: stub format and `<tool_result_handle>` retrieval, `StorageTarget.store` on sweep, the canonical suffix, session log, checkpoints, resume, and both `state.view` call sites ahead of `buildGatewayMessages`.

116	
117	Hard-won lessons from debugging Full CI failures locally. Recorded after diagnosing a Linux-only SIGSEGV in `mcp-stdio.test.ts` (a use-after-free introduced by a per-call arena change, 2026-08).
118	
119	### Reading e2e failures
120	
121	* `result.code === null` from `runFx` means the process died from a signal (Node reports `code=null, signal=set`), not a nonzero exit. If the test also finished far below its timeout, it is a crash, not a hang.
122	* A failure that reproduces on both Linux architectures and survives the shard's bounded retry is deterministic. Treat single-platform single-run failures as flakes only after a rerun.
123	
124	### Allocator-lifetime bugs hide on macOS
125	
126	* A use-after-free of `ArenaAllocator` memory backed by `c_allocator` typically passes silently on macOS (freed pages stay mapped and intact) and crashes with SIGSEGV on Linux (glibc returns large chunks via `munmap`). Green macOS runs prove nothing about pointer lifetimes; verify allocator-ownership changes on Linux before pushing.
127	* The ownership trap that caused the crash: `PromptRunResult.error_code` is a borrowed pointer that `deinit` never frees, so every value assigned to it must be static memory. A dispatch-boundary copy-out that dupes `status_detail` onto the turn arena silently broke that contract. When adding copy-out or changing result ownership, audit every consumer that retains a pointer past the turn arena (search for sinks that assign without `dupe`).
128	
129	### Reproducing Linux CI locally
130	
131	Docker on Apple Silicon runs `--platform linux/arm64` natively (fast) and `linux/amd64` via emulation (build takes several minutes but works). Recipe that matches CI closely enough:
132	
133	```bash
134	docker run -d --init --name fx-repro --platform linux/arm64 \
135	  -v "$PWD":/src:ro ubuntu:24.04 sleep 7200
136	docker exec fx-repro bash -c '
137	  apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq curl xz-utils git tmux unzip python3
138	  curl -fsSL https://ziglang.org/download/0.16.0/zig-aarch64-linux-0.16.0.tar.xz | tar -xJ -C /opt
139	  ln -s /opt/zig-*/zig /usr/local/bin/zig
140	  curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | BUN_INSTALL=/opt/bun bash && ln -s /opt/bun/bin/bun /usr/local/bin/bun
141	  cp -r /src /work && cd /work && rm -rf zig-out .zig-cache && zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe
142	  cd tests/e2e && bun install && bun test <failing-file>.test.ts'
143	```

145	Container pitfalls that produce false failures:
146	
147	* Run the container with `--init`. Without a reaper, exited MCP fixture processes stay as zombies and `expectFixtureProcessesExited` reports them as still alive.
148	* Install `python3`; permission tests shell out to it for `os.getsid`.
149	* Match the Zig version pinned in `.github/workflows/full-ci.yml`, not whatever Homebrew has.

151	### Getting a backtrace out of a crash
152	
153	* Non-Debug binaries are stripped (`build.zig` sets `.strip = optimize != .Debug`), so gdb on the ReleaseSafe binary yields nothing. Build Debug inside the container; the crash usually reproduces there too.
154	* The e2e harness resolves the binary from the fixed path `zig-out/bin/fx` (`tests/evals/eval-helpers.ts`). 155	* A crash PC in heap range with an unwindable stack means execution jumped through a corrupted or freed pointer; on aarch64 read `$lr` and walk `$x29` manually when `bt` gives up.

159	* macOS-local `zig build test` currently carries a pre-existing `terminal` test leak and an occasional `command_runner` timing flake that do not appear on CI runners. Before attributing any local failure to your diff, `git stash` and rerun on the unmodified HEAD; only deltas matter.

1  	//! Projects the within-turn suffix for one model request: tool results older
2  	//! than the most recent steps become a short stub that carries a
3  	//! `read_tool_result` handle. The canonical suffix, the session log, and the
4  	//! recovery checkpoints keep the full text; only the request body changes.
5  	//!
6  	//! Eviction advances only when the un-evicted result bytes ahead of the kept
7  	//! window reach `threshold_bytes`; one sweep then evicts everything except the
8  	//! newest `keep_steps` steps. Between sweeps the projected prefix stays
9  	//! byte-identical, so the provider prompt cache keeps hitting for as long as
10 	//! the threshold allows.
11 	const std = @import("std");
12 	const types = @import("../../shared/types.zig");
13 	const io_mod = @import("../../shared/io.zig");
14 	const result_store = @import("../../session/result_store.zig");
15 	
16 	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
17 	const ChatMessage = types.ChatMessage;
18 	
19 	pub const env_name = "FX_KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS";
20 	pub const threshold_env_name = "FX_EVICT_THRESHOLD_KB";
21 	pub const default_threshold_bytes: usize = 256 * 1024;
22 	pub const StorageTarget = result_store.StorageTarget;
23 	
24 	/// Number of recent tool steps whose results survive a sweep; 0 disables eviction.
25 	pub fn keepStepsFromEnv() usize {
26 	    const value = io_mod.getenv(env_name) orelse return 0;
27 	    return std.fmt.parseUnsigned(usize, std.mem.trim(u8, value, " \t"), 10) catch 0;
28 	}
29 	
30 	/// Evictable result bytes that trigger a sweep; unset or invalid falls back to
31 	/// the default. An explicit 0 sweeps on every step.
32 	pub fn thresholdBytesFromEnv() usize {
33 	    const value = io_mod.getenv(threshold_env_name) orelse return default_threshold_bytes;
34 	    const kb = std.fmt.parseUnsigned(usize, std.mem.trim(u8, value, " \t"), 10) catch
35 	        return default_threshold_bytes;
36 	    return kb * 1024;
37 	}
38 	
39 	/// One per turn. Stubs and stored handles live in the turn arena; each
40 	/// projected slice lives in the scratch allocator handed to `view`.
41 	pub const State = struct {
42 	    turn_arena: Allocator,
43 	    keep_steps: usize,
44 	    threshold_bytes: usize,
45 	    target: ?StorageTarget,
46 	    /// Suffix messages before this index are projected as stubs.
47 	    evicted_before: usize = 0,
48 	    /// Stub text per evicted suffix index, built once.
49 	    stubs: std.ArrayList(?[]const u8) = .empty,
50 	
51 	    pub fn init(
52 	        turn_arena: Allocator,
53 	        keep_steps: usize,
54 	        threshold_bytes: usize,
55 	        target: ?StorageTarget,
56 	    ) State {
57 	        return .{
58 	            .turn_arena = turn_arena,
59 	            .keep_steps = keep_steps,
60 	            .threshold_bytes = threshold_bytes,
61 	            .target = target,
62 	        };
63 	    }
64 	
65 	    /// Messages before `request_start` were already cut from the request by
66 	    /// compaction, so they count toward neither the step window nor the
67 	    /// threshold; the projection still covers them because callers slice by
68 	    /// index.
69 	    ///
70 	    /// Returns `suffix` itself while nothing is evicted, otherwise a copy from
71 	    /// `scratch` whose evicted tool results carry stub content.
72 	    pub fn view(
73 	        self: *State,
74 	        scratch: Allocator,
75 	        suffix: []const ChatMessage,
76 	        request_start: usize,
77 	    ) ![]const ChatMessage {
78 	        if (self.keep_steps == 0) return suffix;
79 	
80 	        const from = @max(self.evicted_before, @min(request_start, suffix.len));
81 	        var total_steps: usize = 0;
82 	        for (suffix[from..]) |message| {
83 	            if (startsStep(message)) total_steps += 1;
84 	        }
85 	        if (total_steps > self.keep_steps) {
86 	            // Sum the un-evicted result bytes ahead of the newest keep_steps
87 	            // steps; sweep the whole region once they reach the threshold.
88 	            const kept_from_step = total_steps - self.keep_steps + 1;
89 	            var step: usize = 0;
90 	            var cutoff: usize = from;
91 	            var evictable_bytes: usize = 0;
92 	            for (suffix[from..], from..) |message, index| {
93 	                if (startsStep(message)) {
94 	                    step += 1;
95 	                    if (step == kept_from_step) {
96 	                        cutoff = index;
97 	                        break;
98 	                    }
99 	                } else if (message.role == .tool) {
100	                    if (message.content) |content| evictable_bytes += content.len;
101	                }
102	            }
103	            if (evictable_bytes >= self.threshold_bytes) self.evicted_before = cutoff;
104	        }
105	        if (self.evicted_before == 0) return suffix;
106	
107	        const projected = try scratch.dupe(ChatMessage, suffix);
108	        for (projected[0..self.evicted_before], 0..) |*message, index| {
109	            if (message.role != .tool) continue;
110	            message.content = try self.stubFor(suffix[index], index);
111	        }
112	        return projected;
113	    }
